summary: Discovery focused on fully air-gapped on-prem deployment for regulated clinical data. Key constraints: no outbound internet from inference hosts, updates via signed physical media or controlled jumpbox, need HSM/KMS integration, FIPS/SOC2 considerations, pilot timeline 6-8 weeks. Hardware preference H100 or equivalent; desire guidance on rack sizing and HA.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25 17:00:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Morales (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ross (CTO, Cascade), Marco Diaz (Platform Eng), Nina Park (Head of Compliance)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, I'm the AE on the account, with Lina from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Elena: Good, thanks. Busy week but glad we could make time.
[00:12] Marco: Hi, morning.
[00:14] Nina: Hi.
[00:16] Lina: Great to meet you all. Quick agenda from our side: understand your constraints for an on-prem air-gapped deployment, discuss update/patching model, hardware and sizing, and then next steps. Does that align?
[00:28] Elena: Yep, that's exactly it. We're evaluating Redwood versus a couple other options. Main point: all our models will process clinical trial PHI so nothing can leave our network, no internet egress from the inference nodes.
[00:41] Samir: Understood. When you say no internet egress, do you have a jumpbox or controlled updater host that can facilitate signed bundles, or is even that prohibited?
[00:52] Marco: We do have a gated jumpbox in our DMZ that can come online for scheduled maintenance windows. It can connect out to vendor endpoints but only from a very controlled subnet. For the air-gapped sites in some of our labs, though, we have literally zero external connectivity; updates currently delivered by physical media and verified on site.
[01:12] Lina: Okay, good detail. Redwood's private offering supports both models — a controlled jumpbox pull and also fully offline update via signed bundles. We have an offline update workflow where we produce a signed container image or model bundle, you transfer the bundle via USB or local network, verify signature via your HSM or a provided public key, and then the runtime loads it.
[01:34] Nina: Signature verification is essential. We use an HSM for key storage and key wrapping, we can't have keys stored on the node. Do you integrate with external HSMs (Thales/AWS CloudHSM-equivalent on-prem)?
[01:47] Lina: Yes, we support integrating with customer HSMs via PKCS#11. There is a configuration where the private signing key never leaves the HSM. For the offline update flow we support signature verification against a public key and optional attestations. There are a few implementation patterns — you can either keep signing centralized inside your security boundary, or we can support an offline signing appliance.
[02:07] Elena: Good. On the runtime side, how heavy is the stack? Our infra team is sensitive about additional daemons and outbound telemetry — we need minimal external telemetry, and all logs must stay local unless they go to our internal ELK.
[02:21] Lina: The runtime is lean. We can disable any telemetry and point logs to stdout or a local file; we also have a config toggle to ship to a local syslog/ELK. For telemetry that's required for health we can bundle it to the control plane only when you allow it — but for strict air-gapped mode it's fully off.
[02:39] Marco: Great. Storage — our current setup is NVMe local for model shards plus an NFS for artifacts. Will Redwood support loading models from local filesystem and not expect S3?
[02:50] Lina: Yes, we support local filesystem model stores. We also provide tooling to package model artifacts into a single tarball with ready-to-run metadata. The runtime can load from the tarball and manage KV cache locally. We don't require S3 in air-gapped mode.
[03:04] Nina: Compliance checks: we're under HIPAA and also pursuing FIPS 140-2 controls for crypto. Does Redwood have any FIPS compatibility guidance?
[03:14] Samir: We have docs and engineering guidance on FIPS. We don't claim FIPS certification for the entire product — it's more integration guidance. We can run the crypto stack against your FIPS module in the HSM. We'll include our security pack that outlines which components have been validated against FIPS libraries and recommended configurations.
[03:31] Elena: Okay. Another point: model provenance and rollback. We need audit logs with who approved which model, hashes, and a simple rollback path if a model is found to have issues.
[03:43] Lina: Our private control plane tracks model versions, hashes, and approvals. For fully offline sites, we can hand you signed manifests that include the version metadata and an approval field. Rollback is supported by a config toggle — you can set the runtime to fall back to the last known good model handle. The audit logs remain within your control and are exportable as JSON, but in offline mode you store them locally.
[04:03] Marco: Latency and hardware. We plan to use racks with either H100s or 8xA100s depending on availability. What are Redwood's recommendations for GPU counts and memory to achieve sub-1200ms tail latency for 2k token seqs?
[04:17] Lina: For sub-1200ms tail with 2k tokens it's aggressive; depends on concurrency. If you want single-request low latency we'd recommend H100s with MIG or multi-instance tuned runtimes, but for throughput with batching A100 clusters also work. For safety, for low concurrency (QPS 5-10) a 3-node HA cluster of H100s with 2 GPUs each (depending on your model quant) is a starting point. We'll run a sizing exercise in the pilot.
[04:42] Elena: We also need GPU isolation — different trials can't share KV cache. Is multi-tenancy supported at the node level?
[04:50] Lina: Yes, at the runtime we support namespace isolation, per-model KV cache namespaces, and cgroup isolation. You can pin models to specific GPU instances.
[05:00] Samir: Quick question about rollouts — do you want canary style rollouts inside the air-gapped environment or will you plan to do manual cutovers?
[05:08] Marco: Prefer canaries but our constraints might force manual. If we can do canary within the cluster — traffic split local only — that's fine.
[05:15] Lina: We can do internal canaries with traffic splitting and percentage rules that don't require external control plane connectivity. The control plane can live in a management network zone and push policies during maintenance windows.
[05:26] Nina: About patching: CVE response. We need a documented process where critical CVE patches are delivered and we can validate before applying. Also SLAs around patch windows?
[05:39] Samir: We typically provide CVE notices in the security pack and then coordinate with customers. For critical patches there is an emergency bundle we can push to the jumpbox or produce a signed offline bundle. SLA timing depends on enterprise contract. We'll surface typical RTO/RPO in the security packet.
[05:56] Elena: Pricing — rough ballpark for a pilot (3 node HA) and then full deployment for 3 sites?
[06:03] Samir: We can do a pilot pricing sheet: one-time deployment fee for on-prem license + monthly support + optional premium SLAs. I'll include a cost estimate for the hardware/ops plan as a range.
[06:12] Marco: One technical nit — our cluster uses an internal air-gapped package repo, and any containers we run need to be signed by our CI before they're allowed. Can Redwood produce signed container images and provide a signature verification step tied to our CI?
[06:26] Lina: Yes, we can provide images and also support cosign or other signing tools. The verification step can be integrated with your CI; for offline sites you can import the signed image and verify signature during install.
[06:36] Nina: Data retention: logs of inference traces need to be TTLed and accessible for audits. We cannot keep raw PHI longer than 180 days.
[06:47] Lina: We support configurable retention and automatic redaction. Also can route traces to your internal audit pipeline. We'll note retention settings as part of pilot SLOs.
[06:57] Elena: On the model side, any limitations on model size or custom weights? We have a couple of research models around 20-30B and some finetunes.
[07:07] Lina: Those sizes are fine. We support model variants up to large sizes; for very large models we'll recommend sharded loading across GPUs and possibly quantization profiles. We'll provide guidance on memory/perf tradeoffs.
[07:20] Marco: For quantization — do you support INT8/4 quant and what's the impact on throughput?
[07:25] Lina: We support a set of quant profiles. INT8 gives big memory savings and throughput improvements but with a small quality delta; we can run evals on your eval set during the pilot. We'll include recommended quant profiles per model.
[07:38] Samir: Are there any other stakeholders we should loop in for the pilot — legal, procurement, security?
[07:44] Nina: Yes, I'll involve procurement and our legal counsel. Also our infosec engineer, Alex Kim — I'll add him.
[07:51] Elena: Timeline: we're aiming to start a pilot in about 6-8 weeks if the initial docs and cost look good. The pilot scope would be 3 nodes in our staging lab with mirrored production configuration.
[08:03] Samir: That matches what we've been proposing. Lina, we'll need a pilot runbook and a checklist.
[08:09] Lina: I'll put together a runbook: pre-reqs, hardware checklist, network diagrams, HSM integration steps, update workflow, monitoring config.
[08:18] Marco: One more: backups of the model store — we keep immutable copies offsite. How do you handle model snapshot exports?
[08:27] Lina: We support export of model tarballs and signed manifests. For immutable backups we recommend storing the signed bundle in your vault and adding checksum validation during restore.
[08:36] Nina: Auditability: we need to see a map of what logs are collected and how they look. Can you send sample audit exports?
[08:43] Samir: Yes, we'll include sample JSON audit exports in the security pack.
[08:48] Elena: Anything around third-party libs and SBOMs? We need an SBOM for the runtime and any third-party components.
[08:55] Lina: We produce SBOMs for the runtime and can provide a pinned list of package versions for the pilot.
[09:02] Samir: Okay, quick recap and next steps: we'll send a security packet with SOC2/ISO excerpts, FIPS guidance, sample audit exports, and SBOMs. Lina will send on-prem deployment doc and the offline signed bundle workflow plus a pilot runbook. I'll put together a pilot pricing estimate and schedule the follow up. Nina will coordinate procurement/legal input and share purchase process. Marco will share infra inventory.
[09:26] Marco: Sounds good. One last technical question — can you do performance benchmarking on our hardware profile? We can provide a VM or baremetal access during the pilot window.
[09:36] Lina: Yes, we typically run a benchmark harness against customer hardware in a lab or use synthetic traces. If you can provide an SSH jump host and read-only access to the cluster in pilot, we can run the baseline tests. For air-gapped sites we'd use offline logs and local runs.
[09:51] Elena: Great. That answers most of our questions. We'll expect the docs by Friday.
[09:57] Samir: We'll target sending the security pack and initial docs by 2026-03-28. Lina, anything to add?
[10:04] Lina: I'll add the runbook, example cosign workflow, and the signed bundle example.
[10:10] Nina: Thanks, appreciate it.
[10:12] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the next meeting invite to kick off pilot planning.
[52:00] Meeting end.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., some proper nouns slightly off). References: "onprem deployment doc (link)" and "security pack (link)" mentioned to be shared via email/CRM.
